scope: physical PDF pages 2-9; all textual layers
source_feature: page-composition line breaks and end-of-line hyphenation
normalized_projection: continuous TeX paragraphs with nonlexical line-break hyphens removed
rationale: These hyphens encode printed line breaking rather than lexical or editorial content. Source wording, punctuation, paragraph boundaries, emphases, and genuine hyphens remain preserved.
reversibility: physical page anchors, exact authority identity, and private crop hashes permit reconstruction and later reversal

scope: physical PDF pages 2-9; French, English, and parallel TeX
normalized_projection: semantic TeX equivalents: source italics as \emph, TeX logo as \TeX{}, AMS-TeX as \textsc{AMS}-\TeX{}, and source quotation marks as layer-appropriate TeX/Unicode quotation forms
rationale: Encode typography natively without changing lexical content; do not rasterize logos or mathematical/editorial text.
reversibility: all macros are explicit in the layer files and source crops remain private evidence

source_feature: portrait image followed by an intentional blank page
normalized_projection: retain the caption and page topology; omit the private portrait raster from delivered readers pending rights-aware disposition; encode physical page 5 as an empty TeX page
rationale: The raster crop is an authority witness, not automatically redistributable reader content. Omitting it must remain visible as a hold rather than silently collapsing the page sequence.
reversibility: VDR-RETRO-ANR-0004 and the page maps preserve the exact hold and source location

scope: physical PDF page 10 / printed v; all textual layers
source_feature: publication-list composition, italics, and end-of-line word division
normalized_projection: encode the list as native TeX description or aligned paragraph entries; encode printed italics with \emph; remove only nonlexical line-break hyphens
rationale: Printed line endings and line-break hyphens are page-composition features, whereas entry numbers, punctuation, bibliographic ranges, lexical hyphens, title language, and ordering are retained.
reversibility: stable per-entry anchors plus exact page-10 authority and crop identities permit reconstruction

scope: physical PDF page 11 / printed vi; all textual layers
source_feature: publication-list line wrapping, nonlexical end-of-line hyphenation, source italics, and mathematical italic l
normalized_projection: continuous native-TeX entries with composition-only hyphens removed; source title italics encoded with \emph; the two entry-[22] mathematical l glyphs encoded as $l$
rationale: Preserve lexical punctuation, genuine hyphens, entry partitions, and mathematical glyph identity while removing only page-composition artifacts.
reversibility: stable entry anchors and exact 1200/6000 dpi crop identities retain the printed evidence

scope: physical PDF page 12 / printed vii; all textual layers
source_feature: publication-list line wrapping, nonlexical word division, source title italics, and mathematical symbols in entries [34]-[35]
normalized_projection: continuous native-TeX entries with composition-only hyphens removed; source italics as \emph; mathematical symbols encoded as $S$, $\sigma$, $S^2$, and $S^{2n}$
rationale: The TeX encoding preserves mathematical identity and genuine lexical hyphens while removing only page-composition breaks; no raster formula text enters the readers.
reversibility: stable per-entry anchors and exact 1200 dpi crop identities retain every printed locus
